messages:
Ivy C: quick heads-up — onboarding CipherLane's LoRA adapter. low-rate failures on invoice-like prompts after int4 conversion, numbers sometimes truncated.
Jon R: can you paste a minimal repro?
Ivy C: `Invoice: #CL-2024-77 total $3,210.75 ->` model occasionally emits only the prefix and then ends. more common with ctx >= 2048 and batch >1.
Priya N: first check tokenization mapping for digits/commas/periods. sometimes adapter merges add a subtle token id shift.
Ivy C: verified mapping matches base vocab. no new special tokens.
Mae S: run a tiny quickpack: `./evals/run_quickpack.sh --model cipherlane/lora --quant int4 --suite numeric --batch 1 --ctx 4096 --dump-attn --kv-warmup 2` and also `--disable-fused-gemm` variant.
Jon R: also try `--sampling=greedy` and `--quant-backend=debug-x64` to force safe kernels.
Ivy C: kicked off CI job: ci/cipherlane-int4-1204 (inference-eval:canary).
ci-bot: job/1204 started by @Ivy C
Ivy C: excerpt from logs:
```
[prompt] Invoice: #CL-2024-77 total $3,210.75 ->
[tokenizer] ids: [4001, 23, 77, 9, 302, 45, ...]
[emit] "Invoice: #CL-2024-77 total $3,210."
[reason] stop_reason: eos
[attn] last_layer_max: 2.8e-05
```
Priya N: eos early + tiny last-layer activation suggests quant scale problem. fp16 baseline good?
Ivy C: fp16 baseline clean. so int4-specific.
Mae S: dump folded weights and run `--dump-weight-stats` pre/post fold. look for clamp or zeroing. also add a unit test that folds LoRA into int4 and does greedy decode on 50 invoice cases.
Jon R: runtime mitigation idea: if a tenant's numeric-extract metric drops >3% route them to fp16 or the safe quant preset. add a canary at 2% first.
Ivy C: uploaded traces to s3://redwood-evals/cipherlane/1204 and will open a PR for a quant-clamp + unit test.
ci-bot: job/1204 completed: SUCCESS (artifacts uploaded)
Priya N: I'll assemble a customer quickpack (30 invoices + notebook with repro/commands) so CipherLane can run on their infra. include suggested fallback commands.
Ivy C: thanks — will follow up with PR link and canary plan.
